segments.he: ועוד אמר רבינו ז"ל מזרח ביים פעקיל היינו כשמתפללים שמ"ע בדרך מחדשין איפוא ממזרח להתפלל ואמר רבינו ז"ל שמזרח הוא אצל החפצים שלו שלא יגנבו אותם. וכשאיש א' מאנ"ש הי' לו היזק או אבידה הי' רבינו כועס עליו ומכריחו לנסוע ולחפש אחר האבידה אפי' כשההוצאות מרובות יותר על האבידה וכן הי' נוהג אנ"ש ור' אברהם ז"ל כשאבד אפי' מטפחת נסע בחזרה כמה עד שמצאו המטפחת.
segments.en: He was for thirty years closed and sealed at Meron, at the grave of the divine Tanna Reb Shimon bar Yochai. At that time there was still no Moshav Zekenim [home for elders] there, and in the courtyard of the holy grave not a single person lived — only he was there always alone. His son Chacham Tziyon Kohen of Tzfas would send him food and all his needs through a driver [a man who had donkeys and would travel once or twice a week to bring him provisions]. He sat there studying Torah and serving G-d day and night, always keeping watch over the lamp. He would go to the Magido — the spring of Meron — where there is a place called the mikveh of Rabbi Shimon. He would go there at midnight and before midnight. And the place is wilderness with wild animals — wolves and leopards — even today, and certainly then when there was no settlement at all. Once he left the courtyard open and when he returned to the synagogue of Rashbi where he always sat, he found it open and full of wolves and wild animals. He took his staff and drove them outside. From then on he endeavored to build a mikveh in the courtyard — and that is the mikveh that is now in the courtyard: he built it.
